## Overview

functai turns typed Python functions into calls to a language model. You
write an ordinary function: its name, its parameters, its docstring and
its return type say what you want. functai sends that to a model, reads
the reply back into the type you asked for, and returns it.

```{python}
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

@dataclass
class Ticket:
    category: Literal["shipping", "billing", "product", "account"]
    urgent: bool
    order_id: str | None   # as written in the message, None if there is none

@ai
def triage(message: str) -> Ticket:
    """Triage a customer support message."""

triage("I was charged twice for order B-2210, please refund one of them today!")
```

That is the whole idea. A few words cover most of what you will do:

::: {.vocab}
`@ai`
: turns a typed function into a model call. The body can stay empty.

`_ai`
: stands for the model's answer inside the body, so you can name it,
  describe it, and post-process it with plain Python.

`configure()`
: chooses the model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, a local model, your
  Claude or ChatGPT subscription…) and every other setting.

`evaluate()`
: runs a function on rows with known answers and gives you a score, with
  an honest interval, and a table of every answer.

`fn.opt()`
: improves what the function sends (its instruction and worked examples)
  from your examples. It never touches your code.

`save()`
: writes a program to a folder with everything it depends on, and
  `verify()` proves it runs somewhere else.
:::

These combine with ordinary Python: a function calling other AI
functions, in loops and ifs, is a program you can measure, improve and
ship as one (`@module`).

## Installation

```bash
pip install functai              # Python 3.11+
pip install "functai[data]"      # + tables: evaluation results, AI functions on columns
```

Keys come from the environment (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`GEMINI_API_KEY`, …), or sign in once with a subscription:
`functai.login("claude")`. See [Signing in](articles/logins.qmd).

## What it stands on

functai is the top of three small layers. You only ever write functai
code; the other two are there when you need to go lower.

| layer | question it answers | library |
|---|---|---|
| program | your function, its tools, memory, evaluation, optimization, saving | **functai** |
| layout | how each value is written into the prompt and read back | [lmcc](https://github.com/MaximeRivest/lmcc) |
| wire | what bytes go to which provider | [lm15](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python) (no provider SDKs) |

## Getting help

Found a bug? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/maximerivest/functai/issues)
with a short example that shows it. `print(functai.phistory())` shows the
exact conversation with the model, which is usually the fastest way to
see what went wrong; see [Inspecting calls](articles/inspection.qmd).
